Not one of the eight fixes in the driver's trace carries an accuracy figure, so under POL-NS-02 every one of them is ignored for this test and counts as evidence of neither presence nor absence. The derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count = 0, rider_qualifying_fix_count = 0 and longest_qualifying_run.fix_count = 0 across the whole trace. POL-NS-02 states in terms that where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. The trace is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, and I disclose that impairment; it only weakens the trace as proof of arrival and cannot supply the arrival the driver needs, because the driver bears the burden of all four conjunctive limbs of POL-NS-01 and has not carried limb (b).

The derived arrival block records longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec = 0.0, accumulated_dwell.longest_run_sec = 0.0 and accumulated_dwell.run_count = 0, against a shortfall_sec of 300.0. And because no qualifying dwell ever elapsed, the 08:51 termination cannot satisfy limb (d) either: that limb requires the trip to end at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and there was no such moment. These figures come from the impaired trace (weight 0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD), which I disclose; a record whose sampling gaps run to 240 seconds cannot be read as a continuous five-minute hold.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-04 is the rider's principal route to a no-fault refund on coordination grounds, and its limb (a) fails outright. Limb (a) requires at least one message from the RIDER during the waiting window whose content is locating or coordinating — their own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that they cannot see the vehicle. The chat log runs from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00 and holds six entries; every one is from the DRIVER or the SYSTEM. The rider never asked where the car was, never named an entrance or bay, and never said they could not find the vehicle. Limb (a) is not met, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider.

Even if limb (a) were somehow met, POL-NS-04 limb (b) is affirmatively failed. The clause requires that the driver NEITHER replied in the chat within 120 seconds of the rider's message NOR placed an in-app voice call before terminating. The driver did both. He posted messages at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45, and the trip record carries in-app call CALL-00901-001, initiated by the DRIVER at 08:47:05 and unanswered after 22 seconds. On either limb the rider-exonerating clause does not apply and no refund flows from it.

POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the platform's own records. Limb (a): the trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 08:43:00, auto-confirmed from a GPS measurement. Limb (d): there is no boarding event, the trip status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, and it terminated at 08:51:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The rider-displacing clauses POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 do not fire (argued below), so the fee stands as itemised.

The dwell limb is corroborated by a clean artifact independent of the GPS. The chat log, at weight 1.0, shows the driver present and waiting from his 08:43:00 message — 'I've arrived at the pickup point, I'm at the lobby area' — through his 08:50:45 message — 'Please let me know, otherwise I'll have to cancel the trip' — with intermediate messages at 08:45:20 and 08:49:30 identifying the vehicle (white Honda HR-V, SGP 4521 M). That is 480 seconds of continuous presence at the pickup, comfortably above the 300-second STANDARD minimum, closing only when the SYSTEM logs the cancellation at 08:51:00.

Under POL-GEN-02(1) that impairment must be stated in the same claim that cites it, and under POL-NS-08 a claim resting on this artifact is down-weighted: it cannot alone support a ruling against the driver.

The rider's cleanest arithmetic route is POL-NS-02, but the clause cannot carry it here. POL-NS-02's own drafting note states that a trace too sparse to establish three consecutive in-radius readings is 'impaired under POL-NS-08(b) rather than proof of absence'. ruling.explanation:
RIDER — your $5.00 no-show charge is not being refunded today, and it is not being upheld either: the case goes to a human reviewer with the money held. DRIVER — no compensation is payable on this record. Both of you are reading the same broken instrument, and it settles nothing.

The charge can only stand if the driver carries all four limbs of POL-NS-01. He carries limb (a) — trip record TRIP-2026-09945 has an 08:43:00 arrival marker — and the reason-code half of limb (d) (cancelled by the driver at 08:51:00 on RIDER_NO_SHOW). Limbs (b) and (c) both run on the GPS trace EV-GPS-00901, and that trace cannot be read. Not one of its fixes carries a reported horizontal accuracy, so under POL-NS-02 every fix is evidence of neither presence nor absence and none establishes arrival; the derived qualifying_fix_count is 0. The trace is impaired for policy under POL-NS-08(b): gaps of 180 s, 240 s and 180 s inside the waiting window exceed the 120 s limb, the window 08:43–08:51 holds four fixes against the six required, and no rider track was supplied. Its weight is 0.6 (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD).

That impairment decides the case. The arrival and dwell facts are carried by the GPS trace alone. The trip record's 08:43:00 marker was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, so it is one carrier, not two. The chat log EV-CHAT-00901 (weight 1.0) does not carry the fact: POL-NS-01(c) measures dwell from qualifying in-geofence GPS fixes, and the driver's own messages record only that he sent them — the clause reads the trace, not the log, and POL-NS-03 reads the chat log only to allocate fault. Where the test admitted no reading at all, an account offered in its place stands in for the test and neither lifts the cap nor stops the impaired trace being the only evidence. Limbs (b) and (c) are therefore undecided, not failed: an undecided limb supports neither the charge nor a refund on those grounds.

So POL-NS-08's closing sentence and POL-NS-09(e) apply: the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under the clause's own limbs, the case escalates, and the $5.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. The same result follows from POL-NS-09(a), because the confidence this record supports is capped at the trace's 0.6, below the 0.70 floor.

On the specific arguments. RIDER, your claims that POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 give you a full refund are rejected as affirmative grounds — the zero dwell and zero qualifying fixes measure the trace's missing accuracy data, not the driver's conduct, and POL-NS-02's own drafting note calls a trace too sparse to raise three in-radius readings impaired rather than proof of absence. DRIVER, your POL-NS-04 arguments are accepted (the rider sent no locating message during the window, and you both replied in chat and placed the 08:47:05 in-app call), so that clause does not exonerate the rider; your POL-NS-05 point is accepted (the trace's minimum distance to the pin is 0 m, so the marker is not false and no false-arrival referral arises); your chat-log dwell claim is rejected for the reason above; and POL-NS-07 compensation is not reached, because it presupposes a chargeable fee and the fee is not established — and escalation displaces it in any event. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is null on this record, and prior_no_show_flags was rightly not substituted for it.

Both sides disclosed the ledger defect, and it is real: the fare breakdown charged $5.00 while fee_schedule yields $4.00 as the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00) — a $1.00 difference, a POL-NS-08(d) defect. Because escalation is terminal and holds the whole fee, I do not dispose of it here. Whether the $5.00 should be reconciled to $4.00, and whether the driver in fact arrived at Tiong Bahru Plaza and held the 300-second STANDARD minimum between 08:43 and 08:51, are the questions the reviewer must settle. The escalation packet — both briefs, the admissibility pre-pass report, every clause relied on and this reasoning — goes to human review. No referral is added: no clause on these facts produces one.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
